Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Paid-revive authoring comparison

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Run REPLAY_AUTHORING_OUT=/absolute/fresh/directory nix develop --command bash tests/replay_authoring/run.sh.

This creates independently runnable Kit and Replay game copies, installs the same paid-revive feature, builds both, and runs three players through the shared contract. The originals and main Replay game remain untouched. The preserved feature patches are applied before test adapters; ownership cleanup of the Kit copy is recorded separately. To open a prepared game directly, build its project directory and run its normal main.tscn; its usual menu and revive controls work. Use the matching built extension through ODIN_SCRIPTS_DLL when needed.

The feature costs the rescuer three scrap, pays those three to the revived player, and restores the existing four HP. It uses the existing two-second channel and 56-pixel reach. Funds and recipient capacity gate the channel/consequence; the recipient's alive state prevents a second rescuer or continued input from charging again. Each variant has an explicit experiment compatibility identifier.

The full matrix has three cases (funded, funding while held, contended), no-delay and 120-ms receive-delay conditions, and two repetitions with alternating implementation order. That is 24 three-process runs / 72 peer receipts. The delay is per process, not a measured 120-ms RTT; no loss/jitter/duplication is injected. REPLAY_AUTHORING_SMOKE=1 runs one funded local pair and produces a distinct smoke marker; the report rejects incomplete plans unless explicitly invoked with --allow-partial.

Test setup uses existing development methods to grant funds and down a teammate. Input uses each game's existing held-revive driver. The adapter only reads state or forwards those operations. The gameplay feature remains in the actual revive path, never in the driver. Authority conservation is checked every driver frame; all peers must converge, and another 2.5 seconds of held input must leave the result unchanged. A missing-funds case verifies three seconds of refusal before funding arrives while the input remains held. Either contending rescuer may win.

feature/feature.patch, before/after snapshots and changes.json identify the feature alone. Counts include added/removed physical and nonblank lines, split by file responsibility. Source formatting and pre-existing helpers influence these numbers. They are not human authoring time, productivity, debugging effort or a whole-framework verdict. Generated code, content, test adapters, copied assets and baseline ownership cleanup are excluded from feature counts but preserved in source/build manifests or separate evidence.

Important boundaries: Kit uses owner-time channels, host consequences and a replicated stat registry; Replay uses scheduled controls and a value reducer for prediction and authority. Wallet/health updates can arrive separately on Kit clients; convergence is required, while conservation is enforced on the host. The u32 receiver-capacity checks are present in both patches; this process matrix uses small wallets. Save/migration acceptance for this experimental rule, broader faults, other authoring changes and human/timed studies remain work.

After all successful receipts, peers stop application and engine networking at a shared barrier before freeing their scenes. An earlier simultaneous-close run hit an ENet send error after its results were written; that partial run is retained separately and does not count as a completed matrix. This teardown is test-only and is not a graceful-disconnect or migration acceptance claim.

The report recomputes line counts and net added library API occurrences (subtracting retained calls on changed lines) from actual before/after files, verifies the displayed patch, checks source/binary hashes, and requires every planned receipt plus the teardown barrier. Run python3 tests/replay_authoring/verify_report.py OUTPUT_DIRECTORY to exercise its rejection cases. The original and primary Replay game files are never test mutation targets.
